title: 1955 AHSME Problem 34
statement: A \(6\)-inch-diameter pole and an \(18\)-inch-diameter pole are placed together and bound together with wire. The length of the shortest wire that will go around them is:

solutions.text:
The centers are \(12\) inches apart and their radii differ by \(6.\) Thus each common external tangent segment has length \[ \sqrt{12^2-6^2}=6\sqrt3, \] contributing \(12\sqrt3\) in all. The geometry of the tangent lines leaves a \(120^\circ\) exposed arc on the radius-\(3\) circle and a \(240^\circ\) exposed arc on the radius-\(9\) circle. Their lengths total \[ \begin{aligned} &\frac{120}{360}(2\pi\cdot3)\\ &\quad{}+\frac{240}{360}(2\pi\cdot9)\\ &\qquad=2\pi+12\pi\\ &\qquad=14\pi. \end{aligned} \] Hence the wire length is \(12\sqrt3+14\pi.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The wire consists of two common external tangent segments and one exposed arc on each circle
Use radii \(3\) and \(9\); each tangent segment has length \(\sqrt{12^2-6^2}\)
